A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable and describe the same Diff-II work, with directly matchable methods, experiments, and displays. v1 includes Appendix A.1-A.5; the supplied v2 ends after the references despite referring to an appendix. This absence is confirmed in the PDF, rather than caused by extraction failure.

before.justification: v1 reports original few-shot, long-tail, and out-of-distribution classification experiments, component ablations, and supplementary sensitivity results.

after.justification: v2 retains original classification results and reports additional Mixup/CutMix comparisons and component-ablation outcomes.

M1.justification: The concept-learning, DDIM-inversion, interpolation, and two-stage denoising procedure is retained. Circle interpolation in v2 Eq. (5) matches the unified spherical interpolation/extrapolation already specified in v1 Eq. (7). The newly explained DDIM approximation and singleton-class noise fallback do not establish a changed underlying implementation.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate few-shot classification on CUB, Aircraft, Cars, and Pet; long-tail classification on CUB-LT and Flower-LT; and background-shift classification on Waterbird. The additional controls introduce no new dataset, domain, or task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 Table 1 adds evaluated Mixup and CutMix baselines for both backbones and shot counts. The six diffusion-based few-shot comparators remain. The actual comparator rows in the long-tail and OOD tables are unchanged, including Real-Gen in Table 2.

E3.justification: v2 expands the component-ablation design with no-concept-learning, linear-interpolation, and spherical-interpolation-only controls, and removes CLIP Score from that comparison. The retained benchmark settings, including backbones, resolutions, shot counts, imbalance factors, expansion rate, and replacement probability, remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Table 4 substantially expands the diagnostic questions from jointly ablating inversion interpolation and two-stage denoising to separating concept learning, linear interpolation, spherical interpolation, and extrapolation. Conversely, v1's supplementary accuracy-versus-split-ratio analysis and additional image grids are absent. The main split-ratio CLIP/LPIPS analysis is retained as v2 Figure 7.

E5.justification: Both versions report three-trial averaging for the corresponding classification results. Neither supplies confidence intervals, standard deviations, significance tests, or seed details. The added comparison rows use the existing reporting practice.

E6.justification: v2 adds baseline and ablation results: for example, five-shot ResNet50 average accuracy is 54.72 for Mixup and 51.89 for CutMix. Retained benchmark scores are unchanged. Table 4's matched accuracy gains are merely converted to absolute accuracies, while new control results are added and component CLIP scores and the appendix accuracy curve are omitted.

T1.justification: v1 Appendix A.1's spherical-interpolation derivations and approximate standard-normality argument are absent from v2. v2 also introduces an explicit approximation in the DDIM derivation and evaluates Eq. (4)'s noise predictor at x_{t-1} instead of x_t. The full-circle interpolation formula itself is unchanged.

C1.justification: v2 explicitly scopes the introductory contribution and critique of prior augmentation methods to data-scarce scenarios, supported by a new distinction between coarse-grained and small fine-grained datasets. The central contribution and claims of effective, faithful, diverse augmentation across three classification tasks remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations about concept learning and separate interpolation components, and explicitly motivates avoiding linear interpolation through the noise-distribution requirement. v1 Appendix A.4's explanation of interpolation versus random noise disappears. The singleton-class limitation remains, while future work shifts toward removing captioner dependence to improve OOD robustness.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project repository URL and documents random-noise generation for singleton classes. However, it omits v1's detailed DDIM step counts and guidance scales, comparator translation strengths, GPT-4-turbo summarization prompt, dataset-specific suffixes, and metaclass list. These details are not recoverable from the supplied v2 despite its appendix references.

R1.justification: v2 expands positioning around coarse-grained versus fine-grained augmentation and adds works including Azizi et al., Yu et al., DiffuseMix, and structure-and-subject-preserving augmentation, plus Mixup/CutMix citations. Some references, including CLIPScore and Places, disappear. The principal latent-perturbation/image-editing framing remains.

P1.justification: v2 retitles the paper, adopts circle-interpolation terminology, reorganizes Section 3.2.2 around the unified formula, and rewrites related-work and ablation passages. The main section sequence and much of the explanatory prose remain closely matched.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column layout and extensively resizes and relocates displays. Table 1 gains baseline rows, Table 4 gains component columns and controls, and Table 2 compresses averages to gains. The retained qualitative figure gains normalized-strength and interpolation/extrapolation labels; appendix Figures 8-10 are absent.

improvement.justification: v2 improves baseline coverage and component diagnosis, but the supplied paper loses v1's theoretical appendix, substantial reproduction instructions, exact prompts and suffixes, and supplementary sensitivity evidence while retaining references to an absent appendix. This substantially weakens reproducibility and support for the central interpolation rationale. The useful additional controls and repository URL do not compensate for that loss within the supplied material.
